fields.description: Your own decision. Whether it is in arrears, due or paid off is worked out from the schedule and the ledger, so none of those is a choice here.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: Borrowed is money you owe, and its interest is expense. Lent is money owed to you, and its interest is income. Every sign in the posting follows from this one choice.
fields.label: Direction

fields.description: Who lent it, or who you lent it to.
fields.label: Counterparty

fields.description: These freeze once a payment has been posted against the loan. A loan is not renegotiated by editing a field — close it and open the new one.
fields.label: Terms

fields.description: The amount borrowed or lent, before any interest.
fields.label: Principal

fields.description: The nominal annual rate. Zero is allowed and means an interest-free loan.
fields.label: Interest Rate (annual)

fields.description: Reducing Balance charges interest on what is still outstanding — what a bank means by a home or car loan. Flat charges it on the original principal for the whole tenure, and is always dearer at the same nominal rate.
fields.label: Interest Type

fields.description: The day the money changed hands. Every instalment date is counted from here.
fields.label: Disbursed On

fields.description: The lender's own instalment figure, if it differs from the arithmetic. Their rounding is not ours, and the paper they sent is the truth. Leave blank and it is worked out from the terms.
fields.label: Instalment (as per lender)

fields.description: What each instalment comes to. Worked out from the terms, or taken from the figure above.
fields.label: Instalment

fields.description: Where the outstanding balance lives. A liability for something borrowed, an asset for something lent — and it is the ledger, not this document, that says what is still owed.
fields.label: Loan Account

fields.description: Where the interest goes: an expense category for something borrowed, an income category for something lent. The principal is not spending — it is a balance coming down.
fields.label: Interest Category

fields.description: The transfer that put the principal on the books. Created by Disburse — until it exists there is no debt to measure, because a loan account at zero looks exactly like one that has been paid off.
fields.label: Disbursed By

fields.description: Rebuilt from the terms on every save, until the first payment freezes them. The last instalment absorbs the rounding, so the closing balance is exactly zero.
fields.label: Schedule
